title: Bikepacking Slovenia – What Worked. And What Didn’t + Final Yoeleo Altera G21 review

takeaways.text: After 530 km and 10,500 m of climbing loaded bikepacking in Slovenia (rider, bike and kit about 120–125 kg), the frame (about 1,470 g without fork, supplied by Yoeleo) was 'a tank': bottom bracket and headset stayed silent.
The only frame weakness he found was soft threads in the many M5 rivnuts; he plugged unused mounts with 3D-printed bungs.
A 2.25 in Schwalbe Thunder Burt fitted the fork with plenty of space; at the rear a 2.1 in tire left little clearance.
The 27.2 mm round seatpost and two-bolt clamp never slipped or changed angle; the down-tube storage boxes were too small for a multi-tool or pump.

disclosure: In the earlier build video the creator says Yoeleo sent the frame and TRP the groupset for free; the descriptions carry a Yoeleo discount code that pays him a commission.
summary: Final review after a 530 km, 10,500 m loaded bikepacking loop in Slovenia: what held up and what failed across frame, wheels, tires, TRP groupset, rack and bags.
